slides.heading: Median Of Two Sorted Arrays
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Searching
slides.narration: Let's solve Median Of Two Sorted Arrays, a very hard searching problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Median of the union of two sorted arrays via binary-searched partition.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Median of the union of two sorted arrays via binary-searched partition.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Binary search a cut in the smaller array so the left halves of both hold exactly half the elements.
slides.narration: Binary search a cut in the smaller array so the left halves of both hold exactly half the elements.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Merge then pick middle → O(n + m)
Binary search partition in the shorter array → O(log min(n, m))
slides.narration: Merging is linear. Binary-searching a partition in the shorter array finds the median in log of the smaller length.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Search the cut in the smaller array
2. Derive the cut in the other
3. Check that the edges are in order
slides.narration: Step by step. First, search the cut in the smaller array. Second, derive the cut in the other. Third, check that the edges are in order. Fourth, median from the edge values.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Partition both so the left halves have half the elements
slides.narration: We want to cut both arrays so the left parts together have half the elements, and everything left is at most everything right.

slides.heading: Worked example

slides.caption: Binary search the cut in the shorter array
slides.narration: Binary search the cut in the shorter array. If b's left max exceeds a's right min, move a's cut right.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Valid cut → median 4.25
slides.narration: Now the cut is valid. With an even total, the median is the average of the max left and min right: four point two five.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We swap so a is shorter, binary search i, set j to half minus i, read the four border values with sentinels, adjust, and return the median when both conditions hold.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O(log(min(n, m))). Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Always search the shorter array and use sentinels at the ends.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Explain the two cross conditions clearly.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Binary search a cut in the smaller array so the left halves of both hold exactly half the elements.
